newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins follow Bradies rise in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins follow Bradies rise in thin trade.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds firmed despite uncertainty caused by unconfirmed rumours that further bonds could have been frozen, dealers said on Wednesday.
Officials from the Finance Ministry and Vneshtorgbank, the main MinFin depositary, declined to comment on Wednesday.
Dealers said the market's liquidity had fallen sharply amid rumours some banks had been advised that some of their MinFins, totalling more than $50 million face value, had been frozen.

A banking source who works closely on MinFin market developments told Reuters on Wednesday that the prosecutor's office in Moscow's Tagansky district had issued an order to freeze almost $57 million of MinFins by face value.
"Trading is chaotic, spreads have become larger as the market is still depressed by these fears of stolen MinFins," Moscow Business World Bank dealer Sergei Kovzharov said.
But dealers said the rise in prices followed the upward trend in U.S. Treasuries and other emerging market debt.
"There is some demand but trading is thin, so this rise is based on tiny amounts," one dealer said.
